narrative:
The model estimates a 66% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors that, in combination, signal a higher risk of departure compared to colleagues who are expected to stay.

The strongest influence is that you have received other job opportunities while at the company. Most employees who are predicted to stay (77%) have not received such offers, so this factor pushes the prediction noticeably toward leaving. The second most important factor is your overall career experience of more than 11 years. While this is relatively uncommon among those expected to stay (only 15% have this level), it also tilts the outcome toward leaving, possibly because seasoned professionals often have more external options. Finally, working in the “other” sector rather than medical or education fields adds further weight toward departure, as this sector represents a smaller share (22%) among employees the model expects to remain.

Taken together, these elements outweigh several positive aspects in your profile, such as feeling you received deserved promotions, benefiting from training, and reporting high environment satisfaction. The organization should discuss retention strategies with you, such as exploring internal growth paths or addressing any unstated concerns. You may wish to reflect on whether the external opportunities align with your long-term goals before making a decision. (218 words)
